Keelwatch · A deliberate maintenance edit.
Real local app, API and PostgreSQL; synthetic data.

Editor A has reviewed revision 1.
A second Manager has opened the same order.

Editor B also holds revision 1.
Both tabs use the shared Demo Manager account.
Editor B drafts a different maintenance title.
Editor B keeps this title as an unsaved draft.
Back to Editor A: prepare a different title.
Editor A chooses Save maintenance changes.

The first write is confirmed at revision 2.
Editor B still holds a revision-1 draft.
Editor B tries to save the older reviewed revision.

The stale save is rejected. The draft is retained.
The server remains at revision 2.

Review the previous title, current title and draft.
Leave the draft unchanged to keep your intended title.

Continue accepts the reviewed revision without writing.
Saving is a separate, deliberate action.

The deliberate save succeeds at revision 3.
The title now reflects Editor B’s reviewed decision.

Activity records creation and the two confirmed changes.
The rejected save adds no successful event.

Activity identifies the shared Demo Manager account,
not the individual visitor or browser tab.

Demo Auditor reads the same final title and revision 3.
The edit form is replaced by a read-only view.

A direct Auditor write also returned 403.
Revision and history remain unchanged.
